Thanks for the flag. A screenshot from a vendor portal is nice but not sufficient for our record-keeping. For vendor classification and 1099/TIN purposes we prefer: 1) an IRS EIN confirmation letter (CP575) OR 2) an IRS-issued EIN notice or bank letter that references the EIN. The signed W-9 with matching legal name is good to have, but we need one of the IRS documents to close the verification.

Until we receive that, I recommend we keep the PO in pending status. If the vendor can provide a DocuSign envelope that includes the signer and signer authority, that helps the audit trail but does not replace an IRS-issued confirmation.

If they cannot locate CP575, they can request an EIN verification transcript from the IRS and provide that PDF. Please ask them to redact any unrelated account numbers.

I can approve an exception in unusual circumstances but would need a written justification and a risk review.

-Vivek
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
